title: August Offer
definition: A proposal made by the British Government in August 1940, through Viceroy Lord Linlithgow, to secure Indian cooperation in the Second World War by promising Dominion Status and the expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council.
importanceInUpsc: It marks a critical shift in British policy from 'no concession' to 'limited concession' and serves as the immediate precursor to the Individual Satyagraha and the Cripps Mission.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of August Offer.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
